_role: Index of the golden System One fixtures, for both consumers of this directory: tests/system-one/*.test.mjs (JS, the two live consumers) and crates/system-one/system-one-client (Rust, protocol parity). Every entry states the file, the wire shape it is an instance of, what it is an instance FOR, and the assertions a parser should be able to make about it without reading the file. Metadata lives here and never inside a fixture, so each fixture file is a pure §2 wire document that a strict deserialiser can take whole.
_origin: SYNTHESISED, not recorded. No response body from api.typesafe.ai is stored in this repo — the router logs outcomes only (~/.claude/skill-route.jsonl carries choice, confidence, usage and cost; never the body, by design). These fixtures are built from the SSO contract §2 wire format, the field names documented in skills/system-one/references/primitives.md, the Laya answer shape in SSO contract §10.7, and the real scalar values observed in the router log (model jev-1.13.0, input_tokens 14748/14708, confidence 0.43/0.44, 115 candidates + none). They are therefore evidence that our parsers agree with the documented contract — NOT evidence that the cloud service emits exactly this. The first live call against either backend should be captured and diffed against these; until then, treat them as a specification, not an observation.
_option_universe: The two router fixtures use the real 115-skill candidate set from loadCandidates('/opt/agentbox/skills') plus `none` = 116 keys, in sorted order. That is what makes the zero-probability re-expansion rule testable at full scale.

fixtures.role: The ADR-2091 router's normal cloud answer: one Choice over 116 options, a low-confidence pick, runners-up above zero.
A `none` pick — the majority outcome in the real log (66 of the 101 routed turns). The router injects nothing for it, and that is a success, not a failure.

All three primitives in one response: Choice, Score (with `legend`, string-keyed `probabilities` AND the array `distribution`), Noul. Exists so the client's answer enum is exercised on every variant, including the Score key-type trap documented in primitives.md.
The error envelope. Carried with HTTP 401; the body has no `answers` key at all, so a parser that treats `answers` as optional-but-required-on-200 is the one that behaves.

The same router question answered locally: 116 options shortlisted to 8, probabilities RE-EXPANDED over all 116 original keys with the 108 shortlisted-away options at exactly 0.0 (contract §2 hard rule), usage.input_tokens counting what the engine actually consumed (486, not 14748).

The degenerate distribution: the whole mass on one option, EVERY runner-up at 0.0. This is the fixture that breaks a consumer which assumes a ranked list has a meaningful second place — formatContext() must still produce one sane advisory line from it.

A compaction-shaped request answered over a windowed state: two questions (Choice + Noul) against 7 windows with 2 selected each, `truncate_left` true because recency is what compaction needs (contract §10.5). Few options, large state — the mirror image of the router's shape.

The façade refusing to guess: the shortlist cannot be reduced below 2 and still fit head_max_len, so it errors instead of letting the SDK squeeze every option to 4 tokens (contract §3.1.5, §10.2, §10.3). A response body a consumer must never see as an answer.
The engine is down and there is no cloud fallback, ever (contract §7). The façade fails loud; the consumer fails open to its built-in path. Both halves of that sentence are contract.
